claims.explanation: Piperacetazine is a phenothiazine antipsychotic that, beyond dopamine receptor antagonism, has been shown to directly bind and inhibit the PAX3::FOXO1 fusion protein in alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma and to inhibit squalene epoxidase (SQLE) in the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway. The selective killing pattern across the listed lines is most consistent with disruption of cholesterol/lipid metabolism and/or fusion-protein-driven transcriptional programs, with sensitizing features including PTEN loss, PI3K pathway activation, and EGFR/BRAF oncogenic signaling that increase dependence on these pathways, while intact FBXW7 and certain lineage contexts appear protective.

features.basis: PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling and increases dependence on lipid/cholesterol metabolism; enriched in killed lines (FTC133, KALS1, UACC62, 786O, ZR751)
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) are among the most killed, suggesting EGFR-driven dependency on the drug's metabolic target
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines (K029AX, UACC62, SNUC5) are enriched in the killed group, consistent with MAPK-driven lipid dependency
Piperacetazine inhibits squalene epoxidase; high SQLE expression would increase dependence on this enzyme and sensitivity to its inhibition
PAX3::FOXO1 fusion protein is directly bound and inhibited by piperacetazine; PAX3 fusion-positive tumors may be selectively sensitive
PAX3::FOXO1 fusion protein is directly bound and inhibited by piperacetazine; FOXO1 fusion-positive tumors may be selectively sensitive
FBXW7 mutations are enriched in the least-affected lines (MKN1, CL11, NCIH1648), suggesting intact FBXW7-mediated degradation of oncoproteins may be required for sensitivity
KRAS-mutant lines appear in both groups but several KRAS-mutant lines (CL11, OV7, GSU) are among the least affected, suggesting KRAS-driven metabolic rewiring may reduce dependence on SQLE
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and is seen in several killed lines (FTC133, BICR6, KALS1), potentially increasing lipid metabolic demand
TP53 mutations are nearly universal in killed lines, but also common in protected lines, so this is weak evidence; may reflect general genomic instability
ARID1A mutations appear in several killed lines (KU1919, SNUC5) but also in protected HEC265, so evidence is weak
KMT2D mutations are frequent in killed lines (FTC133, BICR6, SNUC5, KYSE270) but also in protected lines, providing only weak support
